title: "Real-world tutorials"

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", out.width = "100%",
  dpi = 150, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.6)
```

Four tutorials run the full workflow (tidy the data, check completeness,
draw curves, standardise, model against covariates, partition beta
diversity and report) on published, properly cited datasets. Each tab
gives a short preview; follow the link for the whole analysis.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(tidydiversity)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
set.seed(1)
```

## Taxa {.tabset}

### Insects

Caddisflies at a light trap on the Rhône (ade4 `trichometeo`), 49 nights
with weather covariates. Coverage-based standardisation, weighted
regression on temperature and Bray-Curtis decay.
[Full tutorial](case-insects.html).

```{r insects, fig.alt = "Sample coverage of caddisfly catches"}
data(trichometeo, package = "ade4")
moths <- community_long(
  bind_cols(site = sprintf("night%02d", 1:49), trichometeo$fau),
  cols = -site
)
autoplot(div_coverage(moths)) + ggplot2::scale_x_log10()
```

### Mammals

Desert rodents on the Portal Project exclosure experiment (bundled
`portal_rodents`, CC0). Mixed models with plot as a random effect and
multiple-site beta partitions. [Full tutorial](case-mammals.html).

```{r mammals, fig.alt = "Rodent rarefaction curves by treatment in 2019"}
portal_rodents |>
  filter(year == 2019, treatment != "removal") |>
  mutate(site = treatment) |>
  div_rarefy(q = c(0, 1), nboot = 50) |>
  autoplot()
```

### Birds

Forest birds in Taiwan (iNEXT `bird`) for alpha diversity, and the North
American Breeding Bird Survey (betapart `bbs1980`, `bbs2000`) for spatial
and temporal beta diversity. [Full tutorial](case-birds.html).

```{r birds, fig.alt = "Asymptotic diversity of two bird assemblages"}
data(bird, package = "iNEXT")
birds <- tibble::tibble(species = seq_len(nrow(bird)),
  North = bird$North.site, South = bird$South.site) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-species, names_to = "site",
    values_to = "abundance") |>
  as_community()
autoplot(div_estimate(birds, nboot = 50))
```

### Plants

Trees in fifty 1 ha plots on Barro Colorado Island (vegan `BCI`), with
habitat models, spatial distance decay, NMDS and PERMANOVA.
[Full tutorial](case-plants.html).

```{r plants, fig.alt = "Hill number profiles for two hectares"}
data(BCI, package = "vegan")
trees <- community_long(bind_cols(site = c("ha01", "ha02"), BCI[1:2, ]),
  cols = -site)
autoplot(div_hill(trees, q = seq(0, 3, by = 0.25)))
```

## Which tutorial to start with

- **Insects** shows coverage-based standardisation when sampling effort varies a lot between samples.
- **Mammals** shows mixed models with repeated surveys of the same plots.
- **Birds** compares assemblages directly against iNEXT and betapart reference data.
- **Plants** covers spatial beta diversity, PERMANOVA and ordination.

## Data licences

All datasets come from CRAN packages (ade4, iNEXT, betapart, vegan) under GPL
licences, or from the Portal Project (CC0). Each tutorial cites the original source.
